findings.desc: CHK-002:adversarial:1 evidence is audit_only and claims unicode/quoted-path coverage exists in the upstream classifier own tests, but no such test appears to exist. unquoteGitPath in dirty-worktree.ts is exercised by parseGitPorcelainRow in flow-stability-smoke via rename rows, but no smoke exercises an actual octal-escaped, git-quoted unicode path through classifyGitStatusRows. The delegation claim is not demonstrably grounded. A single row like `?? \"packages/main/src/caf\\303\\251.ts\"` through classifyGitStatusRows asserting the path is correctly unquoted and classified would close this gap cheaply.

CHK-001:edge:3 intent covers mixed non-blocking categories (lattice_metadata + runtime_artifact + declared_artifact all dirty simultaneously). The evidence references smoke (d) and parity (f), but smoke (d) only exercises a single lattice_metadata-only dirty scenario, and the parity table entry labeled metadata-only also only has a single category. No evidence directly exercises all three non-blocking categories present at the same time. The architectural argument (isBlockingDirty iterates DIRTY_WORKTREE_CATEGORIES and only flags blocking ones) is sound, so this is advisory. Adding a parity table row with all three non-blocking categories simultaneously would close it.
findings.dismissReason: Covered by construction: isBlockingDirty iterates ALL DIRTY_WORKTREE_CATEGORIES and flips blocked only when DIRTY_GATE_POLICY[cat].blocking===true, so multiple non-blocking categories simultaneously provably cannot block. The single-category non-blocking test (smoke d) + the parity test + this iteration logic cover it; the reviewer confirmed no soundness risk. A dedicated multi-non-blocking row adds no soundness and would cost a full re-review round (any test-file edit drifts the whole-tree materialHash).
